caption: How I made $230 in under 5 minutes ✨ And no, this isn’t a “look how much money I made” post. It’s a little glimpse into the numbers behind running Signature Hause. One permanent jewellery appointment. Less than 5 minutes and $230 in revenue. Sounds pretty good, right? But revenue ≠ profit. Behind that 5-minute appointment is the cost of our chains, charms and connectors, tools and equipment, insurance, payment fees, marketing, event fees, travel, packaging, training and all the little expenses that come with creating the Signature Hause experience. You’re not paying for 5 minutes. You’re paying for the quality of the jewellery, the experience, the skill behind the application and everything it takes to have that service ready for you in those 5 minutes. I think we need more transparency around business numbers because both sides can be true: $230 in 5 minutes is exciting. And building a profitable business takes a hell of a lot more than 5 minutes. author: 3hmongvn
caption: For the Hmong people, silver necklaces and other silver jewelry are not only valued for their beauty but also carry deep spiritual significance. They are regarded as protective objects that safeguard people. According to traditional beliefs, silver can ward off misfortune, protect one’s health, and bring peace and well-being. For this reason, silver jewelry holds a special place in Hmong culture. What makes this particularly special is that the silver jewelry worn by Anthony Tub Zaj Moua throughout his journey at Mister Global 2026 features distinctive Hmong patterns and symbols, most notably the spiral motif. The spiral motif appears on Hmong clothing and silver jewelry among Hmong communities in Laos, Vietnam, China, Thailand, the United States, and many other countries. Despite living in different countries, the Hmong people continue to preserve their traditional patterns, helping express the cultural connections that unite Hmong communities around the world. In particular, Hmong clothing and silver jewelry are far more than garments to wear or accessories for decoration. Every embroidered line, every pattern, and every engraving on silver carries cultural values, historical memories, and an identity passed down through generations. In a sense, the Hmong people carry their history and culture on their very bodies through their traditional clothing and jewelry. It is this long-standing cultural heritage, together with a strong commitment to preserving their identity, that has enabled the Hmong people to maintain their traditional values across generations. Although borders between different countries have geographically divided them, Hmong communities continue to preserve, promote, and develop their culture. Therefore, the silver jewelry Anthony Tub Zaj Moua wore throughout his journey at Mister Global 2026 is far more than an ordinary accessory. It is a cultural symbol of profound significance, representing traditional patterns, cultural identity, and the pride of the Hmong people. Every motif engraved on silver serves as a cultural mark passed down through time, reminding today’s generations of their roots and the values their ancestors have preserved. This is not just silver jewelry. It is culture, history, identity, and the pride of the Hmong people—a powerful declaration to the world: WE ARE HMONG! #hmong #misterglobalhmong #hmoob #misterglobal2026 #xuhuong
